theory.intro: A straight-line graph shows a quantity changing at a **constant rate**: the same amount is gained or lost in every equal time interval. The gradient of the line is that rate. The line need not start at the origin.
facts: The gradient of a straight-line graph $=\dfrac{\text{change in the quantity}}{\text{change in time}}$, and this equals the constant rate.
The rate can be found from **any** two points on the line — every interval gives the same rate.
The value where the line meets the vertical axis is the starting value.
steps: Read two points on the line.
Find the change in the quantity and the change in time between them.
Divide the change in the quantity by the change in time, and state the rate with its units.

foundation.solution_text:
Hose A: rate $=\dfrac{9}{6}=1.5\text{ L/min}$
Hose B: rate $=\dfrac{12}{6}=2\text{ L/min}$
Hose B's line is steeper, so hose B fills faster.

Printer X: rate $=\dfrac{100-40}{10}=6\text{ \%/day}$
Printer Y: rate $=\dfrac{100-20}{10}=8\text{ \%/day}$
Printer Y's ink is dropping at the greater rate, so printer Y runs out faster.

Point $A$ is at day $2$, level $12$ cm. Point $B$ is at day $9$, level $33$ cm.
Rate $=\dfrac{33-12}{9-2}$
$=\dfrac{21}{7}$
$=3\text{ cm/day}$

development.solution_text:
At $t=5$, filament $=640$ g; at $t=20$, filament $=400$ g.
Rate $=\dfrac{640-400}{20-5}$
$=\dfrac{240}{15}$
$=16\text{ g/h}$ (decreasing)
Filament at $t=0$ $=640+16\times5$
$=640+80$
$=720\text{ g}$

Hose A: rate $=\dfrac{40}{5}=8\text{ L/min}$
Hose B: $0.4\text{ L/s}\times60$
$=24\text{ L/min}$
Hose B is faster, by $24-8=16\text{ L/min}$.

Account P: rate $=\dfrac{180-100}{8}=10\text{ \$/week}$
Account Q: rate $=\dfrac{150-100}{4}=12.5\text{ \$/week}$
Account Q grows faster, by $12.5-10=2.5\text{ \$/week}$.

mastery.solution_text:
Tap A: rate $=\dfrac{30}{5}=6\text{ L/min}$
Tap B: $300\text{ L/h}\div60$
$=5\text{ L/min}$
Tap C: $80\text{ mL/s}\times60$
$=4800\text{ mL/min}$
$=4.8\text{ L/min}$
From fastest to slowest: Tap A ($6$ L/min), Tap B ($5$ L/min), Tap C ($4.8$ L/min).

During the pause (from $5$ to $9$ minutes) the volume stays at $100$ L, so that stage cannot be used to find the final rate.
From $9$ minutes ($100$ L) to $20$ minutes ($155$ L):
Rate $=\dfrac{155-100}{20-9}$
$=\dfrac{55}{11}$
$=5\text{ L/min}$
